newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares fluctuate, seen rising next week.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares fluctuate, seen rising next week.

text.p: Leading Russian shares fluctuated in lethargic trading on Friday, but traders said they expected a rise next week ahead of an operation on President Boris Yeltsin.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares fell by 1.26 percent to 161.38 on $6.84 million in volume.
"Next week there will be a pre-operation rise, but shares will fall on the day we learn the operation was OK," said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at IK Prospekt.
Yeltsin is to undergo heart bypass surgery in five to nine weeks.
"The market is dull, very light volume, practically no orders from the West," said Nick Mokhoff of Alliance-Menatep.
Red October was the gainer of the day with prices rising to $14.50 from $13.65 at Thursday's close.
Mokhoff said there had been demand for Red October throughout the last three weeks in small sizes in the $14.00 to $15.00 range.
The second advancer was Gazprom, which was traded at $0.335 after $0.325.
Mokhoff said Gazprom is exciting continued interest from the West as investors ready for an international placement.
"People are interested in Gazprom as a long-term investment as opposed to short-term speculation in blue chips," Mokhoff said.

Gazprom said in May it planned to sell nine percent of shares to foreign investors through Global Depositary Receipts or American Depositary Receipts in autumn. But Western bankers say the forthcoming issue may be much smaller, at around 1.5 percent.
Gazprom's announement that the tax authorities had frozen some of its assets to force it to pay tax arrears had no major impact on the share price.
Mosenergo was traded at $0.855 after $0.853 at Thursday's close, LUKOil rose to $9.04 from $8.92, UES fell to $0.0715 from $0.0716 and Irkutsenergo edged down to $0.091 from $0092.
